findings: Repository source asks how equals should be implemented when designing JDK String; it does not freeze a particular JDK version, storage layout, or exact reference-class API.

Pinned OpenJDK source independently confirms the current implementation uses identity, String type checking, Compact Strings coder compatibility, and internal value comparison; the candidate labels these as current implementation details rather than timeless semantics.

The reference MyString implementation defines value equality over immutable char sequences, rejects null/foreign types naturally, performs length and content short-circuiting, and pairs equals with a compatible hashCode.

Independent Java oracle checks generated UTF-16 sequences, equivalence laws, null/type boundaries, hash consistency, HashMap behavior, defensive copying, and supplementary-character code units with no hard failures.

The answer explicitly separates semantic design from physical representation and avoids fabricated production experience; O(n) worst-case comparison and O(1) equals auxiliary-space claims match the shown loop.
